Wilson · Regent Brand.com — Accessibility QA Report

Fixed — AA contrast restored

The frost panel now holds contrast against every photo in the set.

Before/after on the wedding-amenities teaser carousel's open (frosted) state. One change is visible on screen; three more are structural and invisible unless you're on a keyboard or screen reader.

Files: wedding-amenities-teaser.html, wedding-amenities-teaser-mobile.html Scope: frost/gradient overlay states Target: WCAG 2.1 AA
01

Summary

Opening a teaser card's info panel puts description text over a frosted, semi-transparent scrim. On brighter photos, that scrim wasn't consistently dark enough to keep the text readable at WCAG AA contrast. One CSS value was raised to fix it; three related keyboard/screen-reader gaps in the same toggle were fixed alongside it.

3 / 4 supplied photos failed AA contrast (4.5:1) in the frost panel, before the fix
0 / 4 fail after the fix — worst case now clears the bar by a full point
1 visual change — a single frost-opacity value, from 0.45 to 0.68
3 invisible fixes — keyboard focus order, screen-reader state, reading order

03

The static state — unchanged

The closed-card gradient (title + meta over the plain image, no frost) was already clearing AA by a wide margin on all four photos, including the brightest ones. Nothing was touched here.

Luxury Vendors
Vendors
✓ Already passing — no change

Even against the brightest photo in the set (the white wedding cake), the gradient's steep ramp to 75% black near the bottom held ~7:1 for the title text. The static/closed state was never the risk — only the frost panel, once opened, thinned that scrim out enough to matter.

04

What actually changed

One CSS value moved. The rest is markup and script — invisible on screen, but required for the toggle to pass as an accessible disclosure control.

①

Frost tint opacityVisual

The only change you can actually see: the open panel reads slightly darker and less airy. Raised until the darkest text (the description) clears 4.5:1 against the brightest photo in the set, with margin to spare on the rest.

background: rgba(6, 5, 15, 0.45);background: rgba(6, 5, 15, 0.68);
②

Toggle announces its own stateInvisible

The "+" button had no way of telling a screen reader whether the panel it controls is open or closed. Adds aria-expanded, flipped alongside the existing open/close class.

<button class="card__toggle" aria-label="Toggle info…"><button class="card__toggle" aria-label="Toggle info…" aria-expanded="false">
③

"Explore" link no longer catches keyboard focus while hiddenInvisible

Because the link stayed in the page even when its card was closed, a keyboard user tabbing through the carousel would land on it anyway — an invisible focus ring, sitting on a link that isn't showing. It's now pulled out of the tab order until the panel opens.

<a href="#" class="card__link">Explore</a><a href="#" class="card__link" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true">Explore</a>
④

Reading order now matches viewing orderInvisible

The description and link sat earlier in the markup than the title and toggle that reveal them — a screen reader would announce the hidden description before the heading that names the card. Reordered so it reads title → toggle → description → link, same as the eye sees it.

05

Compliance verdict

AreaStateResult
Title / meta textStatic (closed)Pass — unchanged, already ~7:1+
Description textFrost (open)Pass — ~3.6–4.8:1 → ~5.4–6.5:1 across the four supplied photos
Toggle state announcementBothPass — aria-expanded added
Keyboard focus orderBothPass — link no longer focusable while hidden
Reduced motionTransitionNot required — AAA-level, left as designed

06 · On motion The open/close choreography (title lift, staggered fade-in) wasn't touched. Respecting prefers-reduced-motion is good practice but sits at WCAG's AAA tier, not the AA baseline this fix targets — treated as a should-fix, not a blocker.
